To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the somatic membrane potential of rat dorsal root neurons is determined by three types of potassium current, which are activated at different membrane potentials and inactivated with different time courses.

the three types of potassium current are found at all ages of postnatal development and that the density of the slow and fast inactivation currents increases during ontogenetic growth, whereas the density of non-inactivated delayed rectifier potassium currents decreases during the first week of postnatal development.

three types of potassium channels were identified in somatic membrane in freshly isolated rat dorsal ganglion neurons: fast inactivating ( A-type ) channels, slow inactivating channels and a delayed rectifier current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogenetic development of voltage-operated potassium channels in the somatic membranes of rat dorsal root neurons.
the development of voltage-operated potassium currents during ontogenetic maturation of dorsal root ganglion somatic membrane.
the ontogenetic aspects of voltage-operated potassium currents, which may be of importance for the maturation of neuronal function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ontogenetic development of potassium currents in somatic membrane is characterized by an increase of the densities of the slow and fast inactivation potassium currents and a decrease of the density of the non-inactivation potassium current.
the fast inactivatable potassium current is the major potassium conductance of the somatic membrane in the rat DRG neurons.

the ontogenetic development of the potassium currents in rat DRG somatic membrane is not homogeneous and that the changes of their densities during ontogenetic maturation depend upon the type of current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ontogenetic development of the somatic membrane potassium currents of dorsal root ganglion is a process of differentiation and not a process of maturation.

the somatic membrane in rat dorsal root ganglia is characterized by three types of potassium current, which have been found in neurons of other regions of the central nervous system and in other animal species.
the ontogenetic development is characterized by an increase in the densities of fast and slow potassium currents and a decrease in the density of delayed rectifier potassium currents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ontogenesis of potassium channels in somatic membrane is not homogeneous.
there are three types of potassium channels in somatic membrane in rat dorsal root ganglia neurons, which are activated by depolarization of membrane potential.
the ontogenetic development of potassium current densities is not uniform for all types of potassium currents.
